threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the 149 is a reasonable route to get anywhere. The locals know the 38 is your best bet for avoiding a two-hour trek.
Last week on the 35, I saw a bloke trying to impress a girl by doing magic tricks. Half the bus was in stitches while he fumbled with a pack of cards.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: One night, I heard a group of kids arguing over whose turn it was to pick the Berlin currywurst spot. That's when I knew I was home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin do you find open-air clubs like Sisyphos, where partygoers dance through the night and into the next day, often with dogs in tow.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s a local when they instinctively move away from the curb as a BART train rattles overhead, no matter how busy the street is.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni in the Tenderloin where a guy was rapping about the 19 bus like it was a love letter. Only in SF do the routes inspire such passion.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think they can grab a café con leche and sit for hours, but in Gràcia, you’ll get side-eye if you hog a table during the busy evening rush.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by how they stand at the corner of Carrer del Bisbe, taking photos of anything that moves—especially the pigeons.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the 'Poppy' in the corner shop is just for smoke. You can spot a local a mile off just by their understanding of that place's true vibe.
Caught a couple arguing loudly about a lost shoe on the 45 last night. One of them was wearing neon green socks. Classic Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I saw that guy planting flowers in a traffic island while the bus drivers debated strike plans over coffee nearby.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a kebab stand next to a vintage record shop, where the aroma of grilled meat mixes with classic vinyl. It's a vibe!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by their calm when a BART meltdown happens—while the newcomers freak out, we just roll our eyes and plan for the next bus.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy juggling on the bus after a BART delay. He stopped mid-act to help an elderly woman with her grocery bags. Only in SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think every bar serves tapas, but locals go for the bocadillos—more filling and way less overhyped.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their frantic search for a 'menú del día' in the fanciest spots, completely missing the hidden gems in the back streets.
